messages:
Anya P: Hey team — FinRelay (enterprise) asked for final sizing + pricing for a 12mo commit. They expect a steady 6k RPS at peak windows (chat + embeddings spikes) with 99th p99 latency < 200ms for chat. Also got a security questionnaire (VPC peering, KMS, audit logs). Can eng-presales weigh in on reserved GPU count and autoscale policy suggestions?
Mike R: Thanks Anya. Quick Q: is 6k RPS steady per-minute or per-second? I assume 6k requests per minute (100 RPS) given their description, but confirm.
Anya P: Good catch — it's 6k/min at peak windows, typical baseline 2k/min. Spikes to 12k/min for embedding batch jobs (~5–10m bursts).
Sam B: OK that maps to tokens/sec uncertainty. What model are they targeting? big-chat (redwood-2-7b) for chat, and a smaller embedding model for vectors.
Anya P: Yes — chat on redwood-2-7b (fp16 or q4_0) and embeddings on embed-lite.
Lisa T: For reserved GPU sizing, rule of thumb: estimate per-GPU sustained throughput for their seq lengths. For redwood-2-7b at avg seq 256 tokens inbound + 64 reply tokens, we've seen ~120–150 chat RPS per A100-80GB equiv when quantized to q4_0 with batching. Embedding throughput ~1.2k/min per GPU.
Sam B: So for 100 RPS steady we'd need ~1 GPU dedicated to chat baseline. For 200 RPS spikes -> need autoscale to add 1–2 GPUs. But because they want 12k/min bursts (200 RPS sustained for 10m) for embedding batches, consider dedicated embedding pool separate from chat.
Mike R: Customer wants price predictability. Suggest reserved commit = baseline chat capacity + 1 headroom GPU, plus burst credits for seasonal spikes. That gives predictable monthly fee and cheaper committed unit price.
Anya P: How many reserved GPUs do you recommend we propose for the 12mo contract? They want minimal runout risk.
Lisa T: I'd pitch 2 reserved chat GPUs (covers baseline + small headroom) and 1 reserved embed GPU. Add autoscale policy to spin up up to +3 burst GPUs across both pools. That handles 200 RPS chat bursts and embedding batch windows.
Sam B: Add KV cache warmup in preheat window. For chat during spikes, enabling prefix/KV cache reduces token compute ~20–30%. We'll recommend a 5–10 minute preheat for scheduled batch runs or prewarm hooks triggered by upstream traffic.
Anya P: Security asks: they require KMS, VPC peering, and log retention controls. We can commit to VPC peering + customer-managed KMS in private deploys; hosted API supports KMS & audit logs but needs SOC2 attestation pointer. Can @Presales Bot drop the standard SOC2 + VPC docs?
Presales Bot: Docs: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2 
Presales Bot: VPC peering guide: https://redwood.example.com/private/vpc-peering 
Mike R: Also note compliance detail: for Private deployments we can offer per-tenant log redaction and retained audit logs for X days as an add-on. Mention as negotiation lever.
Sam B: Autoscale policy snippet we usually propose (example):
```
autoscale_policy: {
  metric: "chat_rps",
  scale_up: { threshold: 160, add: 1, cool_down: 60 },
  scale_down: { threshold: 80, remove: 1, cool_down: 120 },
  max_replicas: 5
}
```
Sam B: Tune thresholds to match their p95 target. If latency increases at 140 RPS/GPU, set scale_up around 140–160.
Lisa T: For pricing: propose commit that covers 2 chat GPUs + 1 embed GPU at committed rate (30% discount vs on-demand), with burst credits priced usage-based. Include overage rate at a higher price to discourage persistent overcommit.
Anya P: Legal & security want us to answer the questionnaire by Friday. Who can take the KMS/VPC doc items?
Mike R: I'll handle the KMS + audit log sections. Sam, can you draft the capacity runbook answers (preheat, cache warmup, autoscale thresholds)?
Sam B: On it. I'll attach sample load curves and the autoscale snippet.
Anya P: Great — last ask from the customer: can we run a 3-day POC smoke test with synthetic traffic next Tues? They want to validate latency and cost profile.
Lisa T: Say yes. Recommend we run two lanes: (1) Chat steady + spike lane to validate autoscale and preheat, (2) Embedding batch lane to validate KV warming and embedding pool autoscale. Schedule SRE slot for the run.
Mike R: I'll coordinate SRE and get the calendar invite.
Anya P: Thanks everyone — please post the questionnaire answers and the pricing draft in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
